body:
[A10] Found by the compliance-matrix audit of `docs/00_MILAN_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW.md` at main 6a878f6 (owner request, 2026-09-18). The matrix Cov column grades the ORIGINAL architecture document; this ticket records what the tree carries today. Baseline at that head: `./scripts/run_suites.sh` exit 0 (30 of 30 suites, 14790 checks), `./scripts/lint_hdl.sh` exit 0.

## REQ-VER-002 (project charter, design) - audit verdict ABSENT

Single-source generation: ROMs, golden model, stimulus vectors and doc tables all derive from one command model

- In `hdl/` today: No command model exists: the only tracked data file is hdl/aecp/desc/example_milan_8.json (a descriptor image, not a command table). ROMs come from three unrelated hand-written generators: hdl/aecp/ucode/gen_ucode.py, hdl/acmp/rom/gen_ltn_rom.py (:12-16 'MIRRORS F05.3 ROW-BY-ROW', a hand transcription), hdl/aecp/desc/gen_desc_image.py. The uPC map is written twice and reconciled after the fact by scripts/check_upc_map.py:4-13 - the opposite of single-source. docs/architecture/09_verification.md:124-127 states the generated environment 'is still the target shape'.
- In `tb/` today: Reference models are hand-written per suite by design (09_verification.md:125-127; hdl/README.md rule 3); no stimulus-vector generator, no golden model, no generated doc table (F06.14, F05.3, F08.1 are hand-edited Markdown). Ver = lint and no gate exists (same search as REQ-REU-002).
- Missing: The machine-readable command/transition/T-constant model of F09.1 and the generators hanging off it; until then at least a drift gate between F06.14 and gen_ucode.py / KL_aecp_engine.sv OP_*_C, in the manner of check_upc_map.py.
- Searched with: tracked *.yaml|*.json|*.toml|*.csv (git ls-files); golden|command.model|machine-readable (scripts/, generators, tb/common, Makefile); gen_|generate (git ls-files) (confidence: high)

## Acceptance

1. One tracked machine-readable command table (opcode, sizes, status set, hazard class, lock/notify flags) exists
2. gen_ucode.py dispatch data and the F06.14 doc table are generated from it or gated against it by a script in scripts/
3. The gate runs in CI
4. REQ-VER-002 Cov/Arch cells and 09 section 8 record what is generated and what is still hand-written

Matrix finding link: GAP-11.

Executor and reviewers: assigned when the lane opens.

[A10] **Re-scoped by the Mark II decisions** (parent [re-assessment](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/415#issuecomment-6009637220)). AECP now runs in two placements: fabric (all-fabric build) and the bare-metal core (Mark II default, parent #665 F5). The single command model generates both the fabric ROMs and the firmware tables. Schedule it before F5.

[A10] **Lane for #73: one AECP command model.** Executor [A595], reviewers [R608] (internal) and [R609] (external). Branch `pp73-command-model` from main `2cbed0a9`.

**Scope (acceptance 1-4 in this repository).**
- One tracked machine-readable command table: opcode, command and response sizes, status set, hazard class, and lock and notify flags, per command the engine serves.
- `hdl/aecp/ucode/gen_ucode.py` takes its dispatch data from the table. The F06.14 doc table is generated from it. Where generation is not practical, a script in `scripts/` gates the hand-written form against the table, and the reason is recorded.
  - The engine's `OP_*_C` constants in `KL_aecp_engine.sv` are generated or gated too, in the manner of `check_upc_map.py`.
- The gate runs in CI. A drift in any consumer (ROM data, engine constant or doc row) fails by name.
- REQ-VER-002's Cov/Arch cells and 09 section 8 record what is generated and what is still hand-written.
- The generated ROMs and the elaborated engine are byte-identical at base and head. This lane changes where the data comes from, not what it is.
- Out of scope here: the Mark II firmware's AECP tables, which live in the parent. Name the export the parent will consume (format and path). Its parent gate is a follow-up lane after this merges.

**Proof.**
- Generated ROM digests are identical at base and head, and so are `syn/yosys/run.sh` and the processor suites. Records are identical.
- Planted drifts, each failing the gate by name:
  - an opcode renumbered in the table only;
  - a size changed in the doc table only;
  - an `OP_*_C` changed in the RTL only;
  - a command missing from the table.
- The scratch parent at dev `e8454e27`, with the gitlink at your head, passes its AECP and ROM-digest gates unchanged. The manager runs the donor and consumer banks.

Post TAKEN, then REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

[A10] **Round 2 for [A595] on PR #174**, head `39cac060`. [R608-1](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/174#issuecomment-6104874774) and [R609-1](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/174#issuecomment-6104929075) are both NEGATIVE. The ROMs stay byte-identical and the table is sound. The gate claims more than it holds: per-command decode and dispatch (R608-1-F1), 10 of 31 response sizes and every command size (R609-1-F1, MAJOR). Hold them; do not narrow the claims. Hold them by construction, not by reading source text with patterns.

1. **Dispatch and decode held to the table (R608-1-F1).** For each served command, the µPC program the engine actually dispatches to on each outcome, and the decode term that selects it (MVU sub-decode included), must equal the table's `entries`. Take the observed value from the engine's behaviour or its elaborated netlist:
   - for example, a directed bench, or the existing `pp_top` suite, that drives each command and records the dispatched µPC per opcode for the gate;
   - or the elaborated design's case structure.
   
   Never use regex over `KL_aecp_engine.sv`. R608-1's q1 (SET_CLOCK_SOURCE redirected to `UPC_GCLKS_C`) and q2 (its decode keyed on the GET opcode) become standing controls, each failing by name.
2. **Every size held (R609-1-F1).**
   - Keep the fixed part where the ROM walk widens to variable, and compare it with the rule's base cdl.
   - Hold echo rows' response cdl to the command cdl.
   - Hold each command's cdl to the engine's decode floor, observed by behaviour (the shortest accepted command), or record the command-size column as held to nothing and say so everywhere.
   - Standing controls: GET_AUDIO_MAP response cdl 20 and 28 (doc regenerated), and a NOPed header field in E_GAMAP, E_GAVB, E_GASP and E_RDESC. Each fails by name, and R609-1's `size_sweep.py` and `rom_size_probe.py` show no passing drift.
3. **Generator-read table defects (R608-1-F2).**
   - The generator, or a schema check run before it loads, refuses with a line naming the command and the field.
   - The self-test plants generator-read defects (message type, entries, status codes, the MVU row) in a file copy, so the generator re-runs.
   - Replace the generator's `assert` with a raised error (R608-1-S2).
4. **Small items:**
   - F06.14 plurals (R608-1-F3 = R609-1-F3);
   - the table as a `ucode.hex` prerequisite in `tb/pp_top/Makefile` and `tb/ucpu/Makefile` (R608-1-F4 = R609-1-F2).
5. **Docs:** the gate docstring, 09 §8.10, REQ-VER-002 Arch, 06 §8 and the PR body claim exactly what the gate holds after this round. Anything still hand-written is listed as such.

New commits on `39cac060`, with no rebase or amend. The ROMs and the elaborated engine stay byte-identical. Post REVIEW READY with the head.
